sections.h2: Where is Vernon, CT, and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
Vernon is the most populous town in Tolland County and belongs to the Capitol Planning Region, which makes it part of Greater Hartford. It covers 18.1 square miles at an elevation of about 390 feet, and the 2020 census counted 30,215 residents.

The town is not one center. It contains the former City of Rockville, the village of Talcottville and the smaller village of Dobsonville. When a buyer asks where a house is, the answer is usually one of those three names rather than just Vernon.

The population table tells a story. Vernon had 10,115 people in 1950, 16,961 in 1960 and 27,237 in 1970. The growth of the 1960s lines up with the consolidation of Rockville into the town, so older village buildings and later housing now share one tax roll.

sections.h2: What is the history of Vernon and Rockville?
sections.html:
Vernon was incorporated in October 1808 from Bolton and was named after George Washington's Mount Vernon estate. Rockville was a separate city, incorporated in January 1889 and consolidated into the town in January 1965.

Most of Rockville is in the Rockville Historic District, added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1984. The district includes 842 buildings and one other structure across 550 acres, with Greek Revival, Late Victorian and Classical Revival architecture. The population of this part of Vernon is listed as 7,474.

  • Saxony Mill and Florence Mill, two of the former mill buildings
  • The Memorial Building, home to town offices and the New England Civil War Museum
  • Old Rockville High School and East School
  • The Tower on Fox Hill in Henry Park

Rockville's growth began early. The census shows 1,430 residents in 1840 and 2,900 in 1850, a gain of 102.8 percent in one decade, and 8,808 by 1890. The mills along the river drew that population, and the village streets still hold housing from those years.

If your house is inside a historic district, ask the town before planning exterior work or a teardown, since district status can affect what is allowed. We have not confirmed those local rules from an official Vernon page.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers near a Vernon house?
sections.html:
Vernon's largest employer is the town itself, followed by Rockville General Hospital. The list below comes from the town's financial report for the year ended June 30, 2023.

Health care, grocery and retail names fill most of the list, along with local and state government. Ask a local agent how those payrolls translate into buyer demand for your street.

Vernon's public schools include Rockville High School, Vernon Center Middle School and five elementary schools. The elementary schools are Lake Street, Maple Street, Northeast, Center Road and Skinner Road.

School names tend to be the first thing a family asks about, so a seller can name the neighborhood school in the listing. Which school a particular address feeds is a question for the district, and we have not confirmed attendance zones.

The Town of Vernon Fire Department, formed in 1980 when the Vernon Fire District and the Rockville Fire Department merged, is all volunteer and runs from five fire stations plus a Public Safety Building that houses EMS operations.

sections.h2: What is there to do in Vernon, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Vernon has a trail, parks and a historic downtown, which give buyers daily reasons to live in the villages. The town's points of interest include Valley Falls Park, Belding Wildlife Property, Talcottville Ravine, Rails to Trails, the Rockville Farmers Market and Arts Center East.

Wikipedia also lists Victorian homes among the attractions, and the Talcottville Historic District. A buyer who loves old woodwork may value a Rockville house that another buyer sees as a repair list. Owners of older homes sometimes weigh that split against a quicker direct sale.

The town also has the Gene Pitney exhibit in Town Hall. The singer was raised in Rockville.

sections.h2: What do Connecticut sellers file when a Vernon house closes?
sections.html:
When the deed is recorded in Vernon, the seller's side files Connecticut Form OP-236 with the town clerk. The state's Department of Revenue Services says that return and any tax are due when the deed is recorded, and that it covers any transfer where the consideration is $2,000 or more, unless an exemption applies.

Vernon's code on the form is 146. If the filing goes in through myCTREC the tax can be paid by authorizing DRS to draw from a bank account, and DRS says that payment starts only after the instrument is successfully recorded. Towns that do not participate use paper copies and a check.

Some exemptions matter to sellers under pressure. The state lists a principal residence conveyed in lieu of foreclosure, a principal residence sold for too little to pay the mortgages and priority liens, a transfer ordered in a foreclosure decree, and a transfer between spouses. A grantor approved for certain state property tax assistance may qualify for a state exemption, but not for the municipal part. A sale completed with more than one deed is taxed on the total consideration, so splitting the paperwork does not lower the bill. Read the DRS conveyance tax page and confirm the details with your attorney.

  • Filer: grantor, grantor's attorney or authorized agent
  • Town code for Vernon: 146
  • Estate or trust sellers: attach Schedule A for grantors
  • Sale split across several deeds: tax is computed on the total consideration

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Vernon?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Vernon removes the mortgage approval step, so the main steps are an offer, title work and a closing date. We look at the address and the condition you describe, then give you an offer you can accept or decline.

It fits a house with a lot of deferred work, an inherited property, or a home with a tenant. It also fits a seller who is behind on payments and wants to understand options before the situation gets harder.

Questions on local permits, rental rules and code enforcement are best put to the town offices at vernon-ct.gov, since we have not confirmed those rules from an official page. Ask before you plan repairs or list a rental.

faqs.q: What county is Vernon, CT in?
faqs.a: Vernon is in Tolland County and is the county's most populous town, with 30,215 residents in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: Is Rockville a separate city from Vernon?
faqs.a: No. Rockville was a city from 1889 and was consolidated into the town of Vernon in January 1965. It remains the best known part of town.
The town government is first, with 834 employees, followed by Rockville General Hospital with 414, based on the town's 2023 financial report.

faqs.q: What is Vernon's town code on the conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The code is 146. The seller's side files Form OP-236 with the town clerk when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Vernon house with repairs needed?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash offer reflects the condition the house is in now, so you do not have to fix anything first.

faqs.q: Does a trust or estate need extra paperwork on the Vernon tax form?
faqs.a: Yes. If the grantor is an estate or trust, or there are more than two grantors, the state asks for OP-236 Schedule A listing the grantors. If there is more than one buyer, Schedule B lists the grantees.

faqs.q: Does the tax change if the deed is split in two?
faqs.a: No. The state computes tax on the total consideration even when the paperwork is divided among several returns, so the total due is the same either way.
